title: WPSS/1351/2013 of Smt Deepa Chaturvedi Vs District Judge Champawat

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
WRIT PETITION No. 1358 (SS) of 2013
Mohd. Irshad and another ÖÖÖÖ.Petitioners
Versus
District Judge, Champawat ÖÖ...Respondent
Present: Mr. B.M. Pingal, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
 Mr. D.S. Patni, Advocate, present for the respondent.
with
WRIT PETITION No.1351 (SS) of 2013
Smt. Deepa Chaturvedi ÖÖÖÖ.Petitioner
Versus
District Judge, Champawat ÖÖ...Respondent
Present: Mr. Ganesh Kandpal, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
 Mr. D.S. Patni, Advocate, present for the respondent.
 Mr. Devesh Upreti, Advocate, present for the intervener.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)

1. The learned District Judge, Champawat was
asked to appear in person. He has clearly misread the
intent of the order of this Court dated 30th July, 2013
passed in Writ Petition No.417 (SS) of 2008. However,
today an affidavit has been filed on his behalf stating that
though he had reached Nainital but due to some urgent
work he had to return to Champawat.
2. On the grounds urged, his personal presence is
exempted.
3. Since the entire matter has been explained by
Sri D.S. Patni who appears for learned District Judge, the
matter is being heard finally.
4. As both the writ petitions pertain to same issue,
hence both the writ petitions are being decided by a
common judgment.

2
5. The petitioners before this Court are Class IV
employees of District Judgeship Champawat. Promotion
exercise was conducted in District Judgeship Champawat
for promotion of certain Class IV to Class III posts in the
year 2008. The total number of posts at the relevant time
was 04. One post was to be filled from such candidates
having Intermediate qualification under 10% quota and
remaining posts of Class IV employees were reserved for
such Class IV employees who were having High School
qualification under the 15% quota. All the petitioners,
before this Court, are having Intermediate qualification
who were considered only under the Intermediate quota
and not for the High School quota. Their contention in the
earlier writ petition i.e. Writ Petition No.417 (SS) of 2008
(Mohd. Irshad and another Vs. District Judge, Champawat
& another) was that they have also a High School
qualification and, hence, they are liable to be considered
under the High School quota as well. This contention was
accepted by this Court and the writ petition no. 417 (SS)
of 2008 was allowed vide judgment and order dated 30th
July, 2013 with the following orders:-
 ì4. In view of above, this Court is of the
opinion that the petitioners are having Intermediate
and High School qualifications and if this higher
qualification is because of the fact that they did
High School, as this higher qualification can only
be attained after doing High School. In other words,
the petitioners are also having High School
qualification. Since they are having both
qualifications (i.e. High School and Intermediate)
they are eligible for promotion under the High
School Quota as well. The non-consideration for
promotion of the petitioners under the High School
quota by the respondents is not justified. This
Court has been informed that as on today, only one
candidate under the Intermediate quota has been
promoted and remaining posts, which were to be
filled by promotion, are lying vacant. Let the

3
promotion exercise for Class III posts be completed
expeditiously in which the petitioners would be
considered under the High School Quota as well.
 5. The writ petition is hereby allowed in terms
of above. No order as to costs.î
6. Meanwhile, instead of complying with the
aforesaid order dated 30th July, 2013, the District Judge,
Champawat in 2013 issued a fresh advertisement, calling
for the eligible candidates vide advertisement dated
22.08.2013. This advertisement is under challenge in Writ
Petition No.1351 (SS) of 2013. This Court, vide order dated
23.09.2013 passed following order in Writ Petition
No.1351 (SS) of 2013:-
ìTill further orders of this Court, the
respondent is restrained from making any
recruitment for the post of class III employee, in
view of the advertisement dated 22.08.2013, which
is annexed as annexure no. 7 to the writ petition.
 List after four weeks. Meanwhile, in addition
to normal mode of service the petitioner shall
served the notice upon the respondent through
DASTI. Steps be taken within three days.î

7. Meanwhile, counter affidavits have been filed in
both the writ petitions.
8. In its order dated 30th July, 2013, this Court
has clearly held that the petitioner was liable to be
considered under the High School quota as well under the
Intermediate quota in the said examination. The persons
who have applied under the High School quota and their
marks are as under:-

 Name Total/100

10. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that
the cut off marks in the said examination was minimum
55% marks out of 100. None of the candidates under the
High School quota had qualified the minimum 55%. Only
one person under the Intermediate quota has been given
appointment and three posts are still lying vacant.
11. The contention of the petitioner is that as far as
the present petitioners are concerned i.e. Smt. Deepa
Chaturvedi and Naresh Chandra and out of those, first
three candidates i.e. Smt. Deepa Chaturvedi, Naresh
Chandra and Mohd. Irshad were eligible to be selected.
However, instead of appointing them, the respondents
have issued fresh advertisement.
12. Since vide the judgment and order dated 30th
July, 2013, this Court had directed that the petitioners
are eligible to be appointed under the High School quota
but it was not clearly spelt out that they be considered
now on the basis of marks obtained in the said selection
but the following directions were given:-
 ì4. In view of above, this Court is of the opinion
that the petitioners are having Intermediate and High
School qualifications and if this higher qualification
is because of the fact that they did High School, as

5
this higher qualification can only be attained after
doing High School. In other words, the petitioners are
also having High School qualification. Since they are
having both qualifications (i.e. High School and
Intermediate) they are eligible for promotion under
the High School Quota as well. The non-consideration for promotion of the petitioners under
the High School quota by the respondents is not
justified. This Court has been informed that as on
today, only one candidate under the Intermediate
quota has been promoted and remaining posts,
which were to be filled by promotion, are lying
vacant. Let the promotion exercise for Class III posts
be completed expeditiously in which the petitioners
would be considered under the High School Quota as
well.î
13. The respondent has, however, proceeded with
the matter and issued advertisement in 2013.
14. It is, however, made clear that only such
persons shall appear in the examination pursuant to
advertisement issued in the year 2013 who were eligible
for the said vacancies on the date of first advertisement
issued in the year 2008. The District Judge, Champawat
shall inform all the eligible employees of the District
Judgeship by issuing letters.
15. Let the needful be done as expeditiously as
possible but definitely within a period of three weeks from
the date of production of certified copy of this order.
However, it is made clear that in case the present
petitioners are selected in the present selection process,
their seniority shall be calculated notionally from the date
of promotion of the person who were selected in
pursuance of the advertisement of 2008.
16. Writ petition disposed of. No order as to costs.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
ML 06.06.2014
